facts.text: Nett Lake sits on Precambrian crystalline bedrock, its basin carved by glacial scouring during the Wisconsinan advance about 12,000 years ago.
The lake receives water mainly from the Lost River and Woodduck Creek, plus groundwater from surrounding peatlands.
About half the wetlands around Nett Lake produce wild rice, sustaining the Bois Forte Band’s traditional harvests for centuries.
An 1866 treaty established the lake’s territory for the Bois Forte people, following earlier 1854 reservations near Lake Vermilion.
Fortune Bay Resort Casino on Nett Lake generates over $30 million annually and employs more than 500 residents.
Nett Lake lies roughly 45 miles south of the Canadian border and 210 miles north of Minneapolis–Saint Paul.
